docRequirement: Shell mode (`!` prefix) must respond by default: `whats-new/2026-w26.md:37` — "Commands you run with the `!` prefix now get a response from Claude once the output lands in the transcript" and "To keep the earlier behavior, where the output is added to context without a response, set `respondToBashCommands` to `false` in `settings.json`." `settings.md:314` fixes the value semantics: `respondToBashCommands`, **Default**: `true`, "Whether Claude responds after an input-box `!` shell command runs. Set to `false` to add the command output to context without a response." `interactive-mode.md:321` repeats it and records the old contract as pre-v2.1.186. So we are bound to two things: a model turn on the `!` output by default, and a `respondToBashCommands` toggle whose `false` branch is context-only.
current: The `!` mode is fully built and hardwired to the documented `false` branch. (1) The composer's `!` branch never queues a turn: `apps/electron/src/renderer/components/app-shell/input/FreeFormInput.tsx:1399-1416` — inside `submitMessage`, `if (trimmedInput.startsWith('!'))` calls `runShellCommand(sessionId, command)`, clears the draft on `result.executed`, and `return true` at :1416, short-circuiting before the `onSubmit(...)` calls that start a turn (custom-command branch at :1421, normal path below it). (2) `packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:16372-16495` `runShellCommand` gates the command, runs `executeDirectShellCommand` (:16425, spawn with `shell: true`, 120s timeout, 64 000-char cap at :16283-16370), builds a `role: 'user'` message whose content is `formatDirectShellTranscript(...)` (:1701-1734) with a `{ type: 'command', label: '!' }` badge (:16440-16460), pushes it (:16462), derives the session title from `! <command>` (:16466-16469), `persistSession` + `flushSession` (:16471-16472), emits one `sendEvent({ type: 'user_message', status: 'accepted' })` (:16474-16479) and returns the `ShellCommandResult` (:16482-16494). No turn is dispatched, `managed.isProcessing` is never set, no agent call follows. (3) The output does reach the model — but only on the user's NEXT prompt: `getPendingDirectShellContext` (SessionManager.ts:16190-16208) collects every `!` transcript since the last final assistant message (`isDirectShellTranscript`, :1696-1699) and `sendMessage` prepends them as `<system-reminder>The user previously ran shell commands from composer ! mode...` at :15518-15521. That is precisely "the output is added to context without a response". (4) The old behaviour is pinned by a green contract test: `packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/sessions.shell-command.test.ts:148-180` ("appends executed shell output as a command-badged user message") asserts `messages` has length 1, role `user`, the `!` badge, `persisted`, `flushedSessionId`, and one `user_message` event — and nothing further. (5) The toggle has no reader anywhere: `git grep -In -a respondToBashCommands -- . ':!docs'` → 0, and `grep -rna -a -E "respondToShell|shellModeRespond|bashModeRespond|respondToCommand|respondAfterShell" apps packages docs-site` → 0. Our own preference surface `packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts` has no such key (its nearest precedent boolean is `useAutoModeDuringPlan?: boolean` at :141, read by `getUseAutoModeDuringPlan()` at :1497-1500 as `config?.useAutoModeDuringPlan !== false`, written by `setUseAutoModeDuringPlan()` at :1503-1508). `settings.json` in this fork is not a preference store at all — `packages/shared/src/agent/claude-settings-store.ts:1-33` is an add-only writer of permission rules into `.claude/settings.json`. (6) Adjacent fork-only hardening on the same function, not part of this gap but on the same lines an implementer will touch: `!` is refused outright in `explore` and `plan` modes (:16393-16402) and raises a permission prompt in `default` (and classifier-selected `auto`) mode (:16416-16421).
divergence: Not a key-name mismatch and not a missing `!` mode. Two deltas. (a) The response half does not exist: no code path dispatches a turn on the shell transcript, so the documented DEFAULT (`respondToBashCommands: true`) is unreachable and our observable behaviour is exactly the documented `false` branch, hardwired — and pinned by sessions.shell-command.test.ts:148-180, so implementing the default means editing a green contract test, not just adding a branch. (b) The toggle has no reader, so neither value can be chosen. Value semantics we must adopt: absent key = respond (`!== false`), matching `settings.md:314` **Default**: `true`. Where the key lives is a fork decision, not a doc requirement: our preference store is `~/.nessy` config via `packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts`, and `settings.json` here is the Claude-compat permissions file. The behaviour is the contract; the key location is not.

Add `getRespondToBashCommands(): boolean` returning `loadStoredConfig()?.respondToBashCommands !== false` (absent = ON, exactly mirroring `getUseAutoModeDuringPlan` at :1497-1500) and `setRespondToBashCommands(enabled: boolean)` mirroring :1503-1508. After the transcript message is built and pushed (:16440-16469), branch on `getRespondToBashCommands()`. Respond OFF: keep :16471-16479 exactly as today (persist, flush, one `user_message`/accepted event) and return. Respond ON and `result.executed`: dispatch a turn on the SAME message instead of emitting the terminal event yourself — `this.sendMessage(sessionId, message.content, undefined, undefined, { badges: message.badges }, message.id, undefined, undefined, { workspaceId: managed.workspace.id })`; the `existingMessageId` parameter makes sendMessage adopt the already-pushed message (:15194-15196) rather than push a second one, and sendMessage owns the persist/flush and the `user_message` event (:15214-15242) — so move the current :16471-16479 block into the respond-OFF branch only, or the client gets two accepted events for one command. Keep the `! <command>` title derivation at :16466-16469 (sendMessage derives titles from message content, which here is the whole transcript, so leaving it to sendMessage regresses session names). Do not await the turn: the RPC's caller (`FreeFormInput`) awaits `runShellCommand` and holds the composer disabled via `isShellCommandRunning`, so start the turn with a `void ... .catch(...)` after the ack and return the `ShellCommandResult` synchronously as today. Do NOT drop the explore/plan refusal (:16393-16402) or the default/auto permission prompt (:16416-16421) while in this function.

blastRadius: Callers of `runShellCommand`: composer `FreeFormInput.tsx:1399-1416` → context type `apps/electron/src/renderer/context/AppShellContext.tsx:170` → `ChatDisplay.tsx:1242-1255` `handleRunShellCommand` (RPC + error toast `toast.shellCommandNotRun`) → wire command `{ type: 'runShellCommand'; command: string }` at `packages/shared/src/protocol/dto.ts:520` → pass-through at `packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/sessions.ts:566-567`. Only test: `packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/sessions.shell-command.test.ts`. Turn lifecycle is the real blast radius: routing this path through `sendMessage` puts it inside that method's turn boundary (`projectMutationSessions` / `sendStartBoundarySessions`, :15069-15082, which throws `session-project-mutation-busy`), the message queue (`managed.messageQueue`, :15227-15238), the `wasInterrupted` system-reminder (:15524-15527) and the pending-shell-context fold (:15518-15521). It also changes WHEN a second `!` is accepted: the `managed.isProcessing` guard at :16383 ("Cannot run a shell command while the session is processing") will now trip for the duration of the response turn, which is user-visible. Persistence: the transcript message keeps its current shape and rides the existing `persistSession`/`flushSession`, so there is no stored-session schema change. The only wire/persistence boundary in play is the optional `responded` field on `ShellCommandResult` (dto.ts:444) — adding it IS a wire change and therefore a risk trigger in this repo; the config key itself only touches `~/.nessy` config read/write via `loadStoredConfig`/`saveConfig` and needs no managed-defaults schema entry.
userImpact: Concrete and daily for anyone who uses `!`. Type `! bun test` in the Nessy composer and press Enter: the command runs, a `!`-badged user bubble appears with cwd/exit/stdout/stderr, and then nothing — no assistant reply, no thinking indicator, no explanation of the failures. To get one the user must type a second prompt, at which point the transcript is silently folded in as a `<system-reminder>` (SessionManager.ts:15518-15521), so the second prompt appears to work by magic and the first appears broken. Claude Code ≥ v2.1.186 answers on the first keystroke. There is also no setting in either direction: a user who wants the reply cannot turn it on, and a user who wants the quiet behaviour has nothing to point at. Two extra frictions on the same surface that are fork-only and NOT part of this gap: in Explore and Plan modes the `!` command is refused outright with a mode message (:16393-16402), and in Default mode it raises a permission prompt before running (:16416-16421).

Two things rest on inference rather than execution, and an implementer should confirm them before committing to the shape: (1) that `sendMessage(..., existingMessageId = message.id, ...)` adopts the already-pushed transcript message and emits exactly one `user_message` event — read from :15194-15220 but not run, and if it does not hold the fix becomes 'append + dispatch' with an explicit event-dedup instead; (2) that Claude's response is an ordinary separate turn — the page only says "The response costs the same as sending a normal prompt", which I read as a normal turn rather than an appended continuation. Effort is M rather than S because of that integration inside an ~18 500-line class plus the rewrite of a green contract test; it is not L because nothing has to cross a wire or persistence boundary unless the optional `responded` field is added. Classified `built-partial` rather than `not-built` deliberately: every piece of `!` mode (execute, transcript, badge, title, context fold, permission gates, RPC, renderer) exists and behaves exactly as the documented `respondToBashCommands: false` branch — what is missing is the second mode and the switch, i.e. present but narrower than specified.
